title: What information can a reinforcement learner use?
description: A short model for the words in Breaking Bellman: data weight, real rewards, and the guess that follows.

title: I made a small game where RL algorithms break
description: Breaking Bellman is a free browser game for learning reinforcement learning. Real algorithms train in your browser and fail, and you fix them one word at a time.

title: Teaching my drawing arm to keep learning
description: After part 6: direct motor drive, learning between drawings, feedback during a stroke, and a twin tested across days. The repeat floor is not a claim of one-millimeter control.

title: How do I get the XYZ position of my robot's tool tip?
description: A drawing tablet measures a pen in a plane. Cameras, marker tracking, and laser trackers extend the view into space, with different costs and sources of error.

title: Where the last millimeter of my drawing arm goes
description: My SO-101 arm cannot see its own pen tip. A tablet can. Here is what the tablet showed: how much error a learned correction removes, which causes are left, and why the base joint matters most.

title: A few predictions about robotics
description: If intelligence keeps getting cheaper, the robotics industry may start to look more like a combination of AI infrastructure, industrial services, and manufacturing.

title: Learning what the physics misses
description: Where a neural network fits in a robot controller. A network that learns only what the physics model gets wrong does the same job as a Kalman disturbance estimate, with more freedom, and this is where recent research is going.

title: A pen holder that shows the arm’s error, not its own
description: I want to see my SO-101 trajectory errors as ink on paper. For that, the pen must not add an error of its own. I made five holder designs. The one I release is a printed sleeve that slides onto the stock gripper: 4 printed parts, nothing to buy, any pen from 8 to 13 mm.

title: Six ways to choose the goal
description: One general formula for the goal sent to a servo. Every controller I built, from a plain look-ahead to MPC, is that formula with some terms set to zero.

title: Seeing finer than the sensor
description: The sensor side of the joint equation: why differences of encoder ticks explode the noise, and how an observer or a Kalman filter can estimate an angle finer than one tick.

title: One equation, and every way the arm misses it
description: Start from torque = inertia × acceleration, then add each term a cheap servo arm really has: gravity, friction, a payload, dead time, a dead band. Each term is one way the arm misses its target.

title: How robot control is changing
description: From copying a person to practicing and imagining: how a robot chooses its next movement in 2026, and what is still missing.

title: Why I am learning robotics
description: The most impressive robots of the last decade stayed in videos because they could not generalize. Language models changed that, and robotics now looks like language models in 2019.

title: How an arm moves: joints, geometry, and motor control
description: From encoder readings to gripper position: a visual guide to robot geometry, servos, and the commands that connect them.
